title: DHCP: Dissect generic encapsulated vendor-specific options
description:
Per RFC 2132 8.4, 'if a vendor potentially encodes more than
one item of information in this option [43], then the vendor
SHOULD encode the option using "Encapsulated vendor-specific
options"'.

Thus, have a test for generic encapsulated vendor-specific
options before falling back to single opaque bytes. This is
done after all the vendor-specific heuristic dissectors, and
treats each suboption as containing opaque bytes.

Actually dissecting suboptions requires knowledge of the vendor
via Option 60. It does appear (#13953) that some vendors only
transmit Option 60 in earlier DHCP Discover messages but not in
the Offer message which has the Option 43. It would require
conversation data to remember the last seen vendor class id to
handle that.

Fix #13953
